analysis.title: All Eyes on US September CPI
key_insights: NY Fed President Williams said one more rate hike this year is still appropriate but he does not expect another hike to be needed in 2027. Markets price 3 hikes by June 2027 versus 1 in Natixis's forecast.
Williams' remarks helped limit the US equity decline and the S&P 500 closed near flat. The semiconductor gauge closed lower for a fifth consecutive session.
US September CPI is released at 14:30 and the Fed Beige Book at 20:00. Natixis forecasts CPI at 0.6% M/M and 3.6% Y/Y, and core CPI at 0.2% M/M and 2.4% Y/Y.
The dollar fell against all G10 currencies (DXY -0.30% at 102.28). EUR/USD rose 0.35% to 1.1192. The Swedish and Norwegian krone were the strongest G10 performers.
Technology led equity losses, with semiconductor names down about 4%. Energy, Communications and Consumer Staples led gains. The STOXX 600 fell 0.08%.
Tech credit underperformed again. Oracle's 5-year CDS exceeded 260 bp (+9 bp). Broadcom, Space-X and Nvidia CDS widened 2 to 4 bp. CDX NA IG widened 0.7 bp.
European spreads tightened against the Bund. The 10-year OAT-Bund spread fell 5 bp to 135 bp, and the Bund yield closed at 3.47%.

JPM Q3-2026 missed on revenue and net profit as softer non-interest income offset strong net interest income. The Corporate Center booked a $0.7bn net investment securities loss with thin disclosure. Guidance for FY2026 and 2027 was upgraded above estimates. CET1 was 13.9% (-0.3pp QoQ) and LCR 113%.

Citigroup Q3-2026 beat. Revenue was $23.8bn (+8% YoY), the best Q3 in a decade, and NII was $17.0bn (+14%). Non-interest revenue of $6.8bn (-4%) was a slight disappointment, with equities weak and FICC strong. Net income was $5.2bn (+40%), CIR 58.5%, CET1 12.8%.

Goldman Sachs Q3-2026 beat. Revenue was $18.7bn (+23% YoY), led by Global Banking & Markets at $13.5bn (+32%). FICC was well below expectations. Net income was $5.1bn (+33%), expenses $11.3bn (+20%), CET1 12.4% (-0.5pp).

Wells Fargo Q3-2026 missed on revenue ($21.9bn, +2% YoY) but beat on profit. Net income was $5.7bn (+7%) and NII rose 5%. FICC trading and lease income were weak, and cost of risk rose 51% YoY. CET1 was 10%, with a $16.5bn AOCI loss (-38 bps).

Crédit Agricole announced the acquisition of IKB (€14bn total assets) from Lone Star. Natixis calls it credit positive. The CET1 impact is about 20 bps, and the deal builds Crédit Agricole's German mid-cap footprint.
LVMH spreads widened 0.5 bp after Q3-26 organic growth came in below expectations on weak China.
France: Rassemblement National deputies will vote against the Socialist motion to reject the 2027 draft budget. Debate on the revenue section runs until Monday October 19.
Apple will launch the Apple Home Collection in December 2026 in the US and Canada, priced $199 to $399, built with LG and Schneider Electric.
IMF meetings in Bangkok feature central bank speakers, including Schnabel at 18:15.

tension_points.bull_case: Williams sees one more hike this year and none needed in 2027, in line with Natixis's forecast of 1 hike by June 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets price 3 hikes by June 2027, so a hot CPI print would support the more hawkish path.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A September CPI print well above Natixis's 0.6% M/M headline and 0.2% M/M core forecasts.
